stem.text: Oil leaks from a storage tank at a rate of L(t) gallons per hour, where L is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are L(0) = 9, L(3) = 7, L(5) = 6, L(8) = 2. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{8} L(t)\,dt \), the number of gallons of oil that leak out from t = 0 to t = 8, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 3 \cdot \frac{9 + 7}{2} = 24 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{7 + 6}{2} = 13 \); \( 3 \cdot \frac{6 + 2}{2} = 12 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.D: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
